patterns.description: Using % string formatting in SQL queries can lead to SQL injection

safe: conn.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = %s WHERE id = %s", (amount, account_id))
vulnerable: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s" % user_id)
db.execute("DELETE FROM posts WHERE author = '%s'" % username)
conn.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = %s WHERE id = %s" % (amount, account_id))
db.execute('SELECT * FROM products WHERE name = "%s"' % product_name)

patterns.name: SQL Injection via String Formatting
patterns.recommendation: Use parameterized queries with execute() method parameters: cursor.execute(query, (param,))

patterns.description: Using f-strings in SQL queries can lead to SQL injection

vulnerable: conn.execute(f"UPDATE users SET email = '{email}' WHERE id = {user_id}")

patterns.name: SQL Injection via F-String Formatting
patterns.recommendation: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s', (user_id,))
patterns.regex:
f["'`].*\{[^}]+\}.*["'`].*execute|  # f-string before execute
        execute.*f["'`].*\{[^}]+\}.*["'`]    # execute before f-string
regexPatterns:
f["'`].*\{[^}]+\}.*["'`].*execute|  # f-string before execute
        execute.*f["'`].*\{[^}]+\}.*["'`]    # execute before f-string

patterns.description: Using string concatenation (+) in SQL queries can lead to SQL injection

vulnerable: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + user_id)
db.execute("DELETE FROM posts WHERE author = '" + username + "'")
conn.execute("UPDATE users SET status = '" + status + "' WHERE id = " + str(id))
query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + user_id; cursor.execute(query)

patterns.name: SQL Injection via String Concatenation
patterns.recommendation: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s', (user_id,))
patterns.regex:
# Direct execute with string concatenation
        \.execute\s*\([^)]*["'].*\+|
        # String concatenation used in execute call
        ["'].*\+.*["'].*\.execute|
        # SQL variable assignment with concatenation
        (query|sql|cmd|statement)\s*=\s*.*["'].*\+|
        # SQL concatenation in parentheses
        \(["'].*\+.*["']\)
regexPatterns:
# Direct execute with string concatenation
        \.execute\s*\([^)]*["'].*\+|
        # String concatenation used in execute call
        ["'].*\+.*["'].*\.execute|
        # SQL variable assignment with concatenation
        (query|sql|cmd|statement)\s*=\s*.*["'].*\+|
        # SQL concatenation in parentheses
        \(["'].*\+.*["']\)

patterns.description: Unsanitized input in os.system() can lead to command injection

safe: # os.system is dangerous with user input

patterns.name: Command Injection via os.system
patterns.recommendation: Use subprocess.run() with shell=False and pass arguments as a list
patterns.regex:
# Direct os.system call with dynamic strings
        os\.system\s*\(\s*[^)]*(?:
          \+|                    # String concatenation
          %\s|                   # % formatting
          \.format|              # .format() method
          f["']                  # f-string
        )|
        # Variable assignment followed by os.system
        (?:cmd|command|exec_str)\s*=.*(?:\+|%\s|\.format|f["']).*os\.system
regexPatterns:
# Direct os.system call with dynamic strings
        os\.system\s*\(\s*[^)]*(?:
          \+|                    # String concatenation
          %\s|                   # % formatting
          \.format|              # .format() method
          f["']                  # f-string
        )|
        # Variable assignment followed by os.system
        (?:cmd|command|exec_str)\s*=.*(?:\+|%\s|\.format|f["']).*os\.system

patterns.description: Using subprocess with shell=True can lead to command injection
patterns.name: Command Injection via subprocess with shell=True
patterns.recommendation: Use shell=False and pass command as list of arguments
patterns.regex:
subprocess\.                         # subprocess module
        (?:run|call|check_call|check_output|Popen)  # subprocess functions
        \s*\(                               # opening parenthesis
        [^)]*                               # any content
        shell\s*=\s*True                    # shell=True parameter
regexPatterns:
subprocess\.                         # subprocess module
        (?:run|call|check_call|check_output|Popen)  # subprocess functions
        \s*\(                               # opening parenthesis
        [^)]*                               # any content
        shell\s*=\s*True                    # shell=True parameter

patterns.description: pickle.loads() can execute arbitrary code during deserialization

safe: with open('data.json', 'r') as f: obj = json.load(f)
# Use a safe serialization format like JSON or MessagePack
vulnerable: with open('data.pkl', 'rb') as f: obj = pickle.load(f)

patterns.name: Insecure Deserialization via pickle
patterns.recommendation: Use json.loads() or implement custom deserialization with validation

patterns.description: eval() can execute arbitrary Python code

safe: # This function is dangerous - use ast.literal_eval instead

patterns.name: Code Injection via eval()
patterns.recommendation: Use ast.literal_eval() for safe evaluation of literals or custom parsers for complex expressions

patterns.description: Unsanitized file paths in open() can lead to directory traversal

safe: from pathlib import Path; safe_path = Path(base_dir) / Path(filename).name

patterns.name: Path Traversal via open()
patterns.recommendation: Validate and sanitize file paths, use os.path.join() safely
patterns.regex:
# open() with string concatenation
        open\s*\(\s*[^)]*\+|
        # open() with f-string
        open\s*\(\s*f[\"'`].*\{|
        # open() with % formatting
        open\s*\(\s*[\"'][^\"']*%[sd]|
        # open() with .format()
        open\s*\(\s*[^)]*\.format|
        # Variable assignment followed by open
        (?:file_path|path|filename)\s*=.*(?:\+|f[\"']|%|\.format).*;\s*open\s*\(
regexPatterns:
# open() with string concatenation
        open\s*\(\s*[^)]*\+|
        # open() with f-string
        open\s*\(\s*f[\"'`].*\{|
        # open() with % formatting
        open\s*\(\s*[\"'][^\"']*%[sd]|
        # open() with .format()
        open\s*\(\s*[^)]*\.format|
        # Variable assignment followed by open
        (?:file_path|path|filename)\s*=.*(?:\+|f[\"']|%|\.format).*;\s*open\s*\(

astRules.description: Reduce confidence if MD5 is used for non-security purposes

patterns.description: Detects usage of MD5 hash algorithm which is cryptographically broken

safe: # MD5 is weak - don't use for security
vulnerable: from hashlib import md5; h = md5()

patterns.name: Weak Cryptographic Hash - MD5
patterns.recommendation: Use SHA-256, SHA-3, or bcrypt/argon2 for passwords
patterns.regex:
# Direct hashlib.md5() usage
        hashlib\.md5\s*\(|
        # MD5 instance creation
        md5\s*\(\)|
        # From hashlib import md5
        from\s+hashlib\s+import\s+.*\bmd5\b|
        # MD5 in cryptographic context
        \.new\s*\(\s*['"]md5['"]\s*\)|
        # MD5 hasher instantiation
        \w+\s*=\s*hashlib\.md5\s*\(|
        # Dynamic MD5 invocation via getattr
        getattr\s*\(\s*hashlib\s*,\s*['"]md5['"]|
        # Variable containing 'md5' string used with getattr
        \w+\s*=\s*['"]md5['"].*getattr\s*\(\s*hashlib\s*,\s*\w+\)
regexPatterns:
# Direct hashlib.md5() usage
        hashlib\.md5\s*\(|
        # MD5 instance creation
        md5\s*\(\)|
        # From hashlib import md5
        from\s+hashlib\s+import\s+.*\bmd5\b|
        # MD5 in cryptographic context
        \.new\s*\(\s*['"]md5['"]\s*\)|
        # MD5 hasher instantiation
        \w+\s*=\s*hashlib\.md5\s*\(|
        # Dynamic MD5 invocation via getattr
        getattr\s*\(\s*hashlib\s*,\s*['"]md5['"]|
        # Variable containing 'md5' string used with getattr
        \w+\s*=\s*['"]md5['"].*getattr\s*\(\s*hashlib\s*,\s*\w+\)

astRules.description: Check if SHA1 is used for git compatibility

patterns.description: Detects usage of SHA1 hash algorithm which is vulnerable to collision attacks

safe: # SHA1 is weak - use SHA256 instead
vulnerable: from hashlib import sha1; h = sha1()

patterns.name: Weak Cryptographic Hash - SHA1
patterns.recommendation: Use SHA-256, SHA-3, or SHA-512 for secure hashing
patterns.regex:
# Direct hashlib.sha1() usage
        hashlib\.sha1\s*\(|
        # SHA1 instance creation
        sha1\s*\(\)|
        # From hashlib import sha1
        from\s+hashlib\s+import\s+.*\bsha1\b|
        # SHA1 in cryptographic context
        \.new\s*\(\s*['"]sha1['"]\s*\)|
        # SHA1 hasher instantiation
        \w+\s*=\s*hashlib\.sha1\s*\(|
        # hashlib.sha1 as parameter (without parentheses)
        hashlib\.sha1\b
regexPatterns:
# Direct hashlib.sha1() usage
        hashlib\.sha1\s*\(|
        # SHA1 instance creation
        sha1\s*\(\)|
        # From hashlib import sha1
        from\s+hashlib\s+import\s+.*\bsha1\b|
        # SHA1 in cryptographic context
        \.new\s*\(\s*['"]sha1['"]\s*\)|
        # SHA1 hasher instantiation
        \w+\s*=\s*hashlib\.sha1\s*\(|
        # hashlib.sha1 as parameter (without parentheses)
        hashlib\.sha1\b

patterns.description: Detects when DEBUG is set to True, which can expose sensitive information in production
patterns.name: Debug Mode Enabled
patterns.recommendation: Set DEBUG = False in production environments
patterns.regex:
# Direct DEBUG = True assignment
        DEBUG\s*=\s*True|
        # Settings with DEBUG = True
        settings\.DEBUG\s*=\s*True|
        # Configuration dictionary with debug True
        ['"]debug['"]\s*:\s*True|
        # Environment variable defaulting to True
        os\.environ\.get\s*\(\s*['"]DEBUG['"]\s*,\s*(?:True|['"]True['"])\s*\)|
        # Config object with debug = True
        \.debug\s*=\s*True|
        # app.debug = True (Flask)
        app\.debug\s*=\s*True|
        # app.run(debug=True) (Flask)
        \.run\(.*debug\s*=\s*True
regexPatterns:
# Direct DEBUG = True assignment
        DEBUG\s*=\s*True|
        # Settings with DEBUG = True
        settings\.DEBUG\s*=\s*True|
        # Configuration dictionary with debug True
        ['"]debug['"]\s*:\s*True|
        # Environment variable defaulting to True
        os\.environ\.get\s*\(\s*['"]DEBUG['"]\s*,\s*(?:True|['"]True['"])\s*\)|
        # Config object with debug = True
        \.debug\s*=\s*True|
        # app.debug = True (Flask)
        app\.debug\s*=\s*True|
        # app.run(debug=True) (Flask)
        \.run\(.*debug\s*=\s*True

patterns.description: Detects unsafe usage of yaml.load() which can execute arbitrary Python code

vulnerable: from yaml import load; data = load(request.body)

patterns.name: Unsafe YAML Deserialization
patterns.recommendation: Use yaml.safe_load() or yaml.load(data, Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)
patterns.regex:
# yaml.load() without SafeLoader or with FullLoader
        yaml\.load\s*\((?:[^,)]|,\s*Loader\s*=\s*yaml\.FullLoader)*\)|
        # from yaml import load
        from\s+yaml\s+import\s+.*\bload\b|
        # Direct load() call after import
        (?:^|\s)load\s*\([^,)]*\)
regexPatterns:
# yaml.load() without SafeLoader or with FullLoader
        yaml\.load\s*\((?:[^,)]|,\s*Loader\s*=\s*yaml\.FullLoader)*\)|
        # from yaml import load
        from\s+yaml\s+import\s+.*\bload\b|
        # Direct load() call after import
        (?:^|\s)load\s*\([^,)]*\)

patterns.description: User input passed to render_template_string() enables Jinja2 template injection and code execution
patterns.name: Server-Side Template Injection via render_template_string()
patterns.recommendation: Use render_template() with a static template file and pass user data as template variables, not as the template string itself

patterns.description: JWT signature verification disabled, allowing token forgery and authentication bypass

vulnerable: decoded = jwt.decode(token, key, options={"verify_exp": False, "verify_signature": False})

patterns.name: Insecure JWT Verification
patterns.recommendation: Always verify JWT signatures: jwt.decode(token, secret_key, algorithms=['HS256']). Never use verify=False or allow the 'none' algorithm.

patterns.description: Detects hardcoded API keys, passwords, secrets, and credentials in Python code
patterns.name: Hardcoded Secrets
patterns.recommendation: Store secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager. Use os.environ.get() or python-dotenv for configuration.

patterns.description: SQL injection through Django ORM using string formatting

vulnerable: User.objects.raw("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '%s'" % name)
cursor.execute("DELETE FROM table WHERE id = %s" % user_id)

patterns.name: Django ORM SQL Injection
patterns.recommendation: Use Django parameterized queries: Model.objects.raw("SELECT * FROM table WHERE id = %s", [user_id]) or Django ORM methods: filter(name=username)

patterns.description: NoSQL injection through MongoDB, Elasticsearch, or Redis with user input
patterns.name: Django NoSQL Injection
patterns.recommendation: Validate and sanitize user input before using in NoSQL queries. Use parameterized queries where possible.

patterns.description: XSS vulnerabilities through unsafe Django template filters
patterns.name: Django Template XSS
patterns.recommendation: Avoid using |safe filter on user input. Use Django's built-in escaping. If HTML is needed, sanitize with bleach library.

patterns.description: Server-side template injection allowing code execution
patterns.name: Django Template Injection
patterns.recommendation: Never render user input as template code. Use static template names only.

patterns.description: Debug mode exposes sensitive information in production
patterns.name: Django Debug Mode in Production
patterns.recommendation: Set DEBUG = False in production settings. Use environment-specific settings files.

patterns.description: Session cookies without secure flags expose sessions to interception
patterns.name: Django Insecure Session Configuration
patterns.recommendation: Enable secure session cookies: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True, SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = 'Strict'

patterns.description: Missing important security middleware in Django settings
patterns.name: Django Missing Security Middleware
patterns.recommendation: Add security middleware: django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware, django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware, and django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware

patterns.description: Weak or missing authentication checks in Django views
patterns.name: Django Broken Authentication
patterns.recommendation: Use @login_required decorator or LoginRequiredMixin for views requiring authentication

patterns.description: Missing or insufficient permission checks allowing unauthorized access
patterns.name: Django Authorization Bypass
patterns.recommendation: Implement proper permission checks using @permission_required or check user.has_perm()

patterns.description: CSRF protection disabled or bypassed

safe:
def payment_view(request):
    # CSRF protected by default

patterns.name: Django CSRF Bypass
patterns.recommendation: Enable CSRF protection. Only use @csrf_exempt when absolutely necessary with additional security measures.

patterns.description: Missing X-Frame-Options header protection
patterns.name: Django Clickjacking Vulnerability
patterns.recommendation: Set X_FRAME_OPTIONS = 'DENY' in settings

patterns.description: Injection vulnerabilities in model operations

model.save(update_fields=[f for f in fields if f in allowed_fields])

patterns.name: Django Model Injection
patterns.recommendation: Validate and whitelist fields before model operations

patterns.description: Mass assignment allowing unauthorized field updates
patterns.name: Django Mass Assignment
patterns.recommendation: Explicitly define allowed fields in forms and serializers

patterns.description: URL patterns that may expose sensitive endpoints
patterns.name: Django Unsafe URL Patterns
patterns.recommendation: Use specific URL patterns. Change default admin URL. Remove debug tools in production.
